transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Rohit Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Novella, CTO), Liam O'Connor (Novella, ML Eng), Priya Singh (Novella, Product)

Summary:
- Discovery to understand embeddings + rerank use case, vector DB integrations, throughput requirements, and security needs.
- Novella evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for production reranking and semantic search; currently prototyping with Elastic + open-source embedding pipeline.
- Agreed next steps: share pricing, security docs, run a 2-week benchmark with sample data.

Topics:
- Vector DB options (Pinecone/Weaviate/Qdrant/Milvus)
- Embedding dimensionality and model choice (512/1024/1536)
- Hybrid search (BM25 + dense embedding rerank)
- Throughput (QPS), batching, and latency SLOs
- Security: SOC2, VPC, KMS, audit logs

Transcript body:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're excited to learn about Novella's reranking work today, quick intros?
[00:12] Maya Chen: Hi, Maya here, CTO, we run the search stack and infra.
[00:16] Liam O'Connor: Liam, ML eng, building the embed and rerank pipelines.
[00:20] Priya Singh: Priya, product, I'll handle success criteria and stakeholder side.
[00:25] Ava Martinez: Great, I'm Ava on the AE side and Rohit--
[00:28] Rohit Patel: --hi all, Rohit SE, I'll cover latency and throughput and integration details.
[00:33] Maya Chen: Cool. Quick context: we've been prototyping semantic search on top of Elastic, using a 768-d embed from an open model, initial results ok but rerank quality and scale are limiting.
[00:45] Liam O'Connor: Yeah and we're hitting issues at about 150 QPS during peak, rerank latencies blow up since we do a kNN fetch + re-rank transformer.
[00:53] Rohit Patel: Makes sense. Are you doing hybrid search (BM25 then dense) or pure vector?
[00:58] Liam O'Connor: Hybrid today — BM25 to narrow, then dense rerank. We want to push to 500 QPS target and keep tail latency < 150 ms for the rerank step.
[01:10] Ava Martinez: Good number to shoot for. Can you describe your vector DB and embedding pipeline?
[01:15] Liam O'Connor: Right now it's Elastic vector fields + our job that produces 768-d embeddings via open model hosted in our infra, storing vectors in ES nodes, but it's not optimized. We're looking at Pinecone and Milvus for better kNN.
[01:27] Priya Singh: Also security is a big factor — some of our clients need data residency and strict key management.
[01:33] Maya Chen: SOC2 and audit logs are must-haves.
[01:36] Rohit Patel: Understood. On Redwood side we have three deployment modes — Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem). Hosted is quickest to start, Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation, Private gives full network control and KMS/HSM options.
[01:52] Maya Chen: For Dedicated, is it single-tenant GPU pools? We need predictable latency under load.
[01:57] Rohit Patel: Yes, Dedicated gives reserved GPU capacity per customer and we can configure autoscale behavior and burst policies. For strict latency SLOs we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[02:07] Liam O'Connor: How do you handle embedding dimensionality? We may move to 1024 or 1536 dims depending on model — curious about throughput impact.
[02:16] Rohit Patel: Higher dimensionality increases compute and memory for the serving runtime and also affects vector DB storage/NN search cost. For Redwood serving we optimize kernels, but you should expect linear-ish cost jumps from 768→1024→1536. We often recommend 1024 as a balance.
[02:31] Priya Singh: And for rerank, do you handle on-server cross-encoder re-rank or is this separate?
[02:36] Rohit Patel: We support both. For cheap fast rerank you can do a lightweight MLP on top of embeddings. For cross-encoder you can run a transformer via Redwood generation endpoints — that has higher latency. Many customers do a two-phase: dense kNN recall then a cross-encoder rerank on top-k (k=10-50).
[02:52] Ava Martinez: One pattern we see is doing a narrow recall with sparse signals (BM25) then embed-based recall, then a small cross-encoder rerank on the top 20. Keeps quality high while bounding cost.
[03:03] Maya Chen: That aligns with our thinking. The tricky part is throughput — cross-encoder at 500 QPS seems expensive.
[03:09] Liam O'Connor: Yeah cost is a constraint. We're trying to quantify tradeoffs.
[03:13] Rohit Patel: For cost/perf we have Redwood Optimize suggestions— quantize models, tune batching, and use prefix/KV caching. Also routing policies can fallback to cheaper model variants if needed.
[03:26] Priya Singh: About vector DB connectors — do you recommend integrating with Pinecone or doing direct Redwood retrieval?
[03:31] Rohit Patel: Redwood doesn't replace vector DBs; we serve embeddings and can integrate with any vector DB. We have connectors and best-practice configs for Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant, Milvus, and even Elastic vectors. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can co-locate the embedding serving near the DB to reduce cross-network latency.
[03:49] Maya Chen: Any specific limits on dimensionality per connector? Pinecone seems to support higher dims but costs scale.
[03:54] Rohit Patel: Most DBs support up to several thousand dims but index type matters (HNSW vs IVFPQ). Also compression/quantization at index time matters. We can share sample configs.
[04:05] Liam O'Connor: On indexing strategy — we're interested in hybrid search where we combine BM25 score + cosine sim; do you have recommendations for score normalization?
[04:13] Rohit Patel: Normalize both signals to 0-1 and use tunable weights. If you have business labels you can train a small ranker to combine features; Redwood's rollout tooling helps validate A/Bs.
[04:24] Ava Martinez: Question on latency SLOs: you said 150 ms for rerank tail — is that end-to-end?
[04:29] Liam O'Connor: That's for the rerank step only, not including BM25 recall.
[04:33] Rohit Patel: For that tail you likely need Dedicated or Private plus optimized batching. Single-request cross-encoders will be expensive; batched cross-encoder inference coupled with KV caching for repeated prefixes helps.
[04:47] Maya Chen: What about cold starts and model warm-up? On our side we see spikes after deploys.
[04:53] Rohit Patel: We recommend pre-warming, and for Dedicated there's an option to keep a minimum pool warm. Also our runtime supports dynamic kernel selection to speed warm-up.
[05:05] Priya Singh: Security — can you walk through KMS integration and audit logs briefly?
[05:10] Rohit Patel: Sure. For Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or HSM) for key material. Audit logs are available via our console and can be exported to S3 or a SIEM. Hosted customers get SOC2 controls and per-token cost/latency breakdowns.
[05:24] Maya Chen: Is SAML SSO available for the console?
[05:27] Ava Martinez: Yes SSO/SAML and RBAC are available; we'll include the security pack in the follow-up.
[05:33] Liam O'Connor: On the practical side — we have a dataset of ~10M docs, average doc embedding count ~2 per doc, so ~20M vectors. Storage and search cost estimation?
[05:44] Rohit Patel: For 20M vectors at 1024 dims, you'll want an index type with compressed storage; Milvus/Qdrant with IVFPQ helps. Storage and QPS cost estimates depend on chosen index and replicas. We'll include sample cost models.
[05:58] Priya Singh: Do you run benchmarks for customers?
[06:01] Ava Martinez: Yes, we can run a 2-week benchmark on Dedicated or Private. Rohit will share a template for QPS/latency targets and dataset ingestion steps.
[06:11] Rohit Patel: I'll share the benchmark template and some scripts for ingesting to common DBs.
[06:16] Maya Chen: For the benchmark, we want to test 400-600 QPS with hybrid recall and top-20 cross-encoder rerank, as a stress scenario.
[06:25] Rohit Patel: That's doable; we'll size a Dedicated pool for that and simulate burst traffic.
[06:30] Liam O'Connor: Any constraints around private on-prem? We have some on-prem infra for regulated clients.
[06:35] Rohit Patel: Private supports on-prem packages with an air-gapped option; we can run the control plane in your VPC and the inference nodes inside your network. KMS/HSM integration and audit log exports are supported. There are additional ops and licensing conversations for on-prem.
[06:50] Maya Chen: Good to hear. Another practical: connector latency between Redwood serving and external vector DB — if we co-locate, is there a recommended network topology?
[06:59] Rohit Patel: Co-locate in same region and same VPC/subnet, use private peering. For Dedicated we can provision nodes in the same availability zone as your DB replicas.
[07:10] Priya Singh: Costs again — do you have ballpark numbers for Dedicated versus Hosted for a 20M-vector, 500 QPS workload?
[07:18] Ava Martinez: We'll send a tailored pricing sheet but rough guidance: Hosted is cheaper to start but at sustained 500 QPS Dedicated often becomes more economical due to reserved capacity. We'll include a TCO comparison.
[07:30] Liam O'Connor: In terms of embedding model we plan to test 768 vs 1024 dims, and perhaps a 2048 model for research. Does Redwood support custom models?
[07:38] Rohit Patel: Yes, you can bring your own model (BYOM). For Hosted we support curated open models. For Dedicated/Private we can deploy your model artifact and help with quantization and kernel tuning.
[07:50] Maya Chen: Do you have built-in evals for quality regressions? We want to avoid a drop in rerank quality after swaps.
[07:56] Ava Martinez: Redwood Optimize includes eval hooks tied to prompt sets and quality monitoring, and you can set regression alerts. We'll share an eval checklist.
[08:06] Priya Singh: On SLOs and retries — how does Redwood handle degraded capacity or fallback?
[08:11] Rohit Patel: Smart routing can fallback to cheaper model variants or a lower-cost region, and we support automatic retries and circuit-breaker behaviors. We also offer canary rollouts and A/B testing.
[08:23] Liam O'Connor: Any caveats with KV caching and rerank — if we cache top candidates, we might reduce cross-encoder calls but need cache invalidation.
[08:32] Rohit Patel: Yep. We recommend short TTLs for high-update corpora and prefix-based invalidation for predictable patterns. The runtime exposes hooks for your application to control cache keys.
[08:44] Maya Chen: Let's talk SLAs — what uptime guarantees exist for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[08:50] Ava Martinez: Hosted has a standard availability target; Dedicated can be SLA-backed depending on contract. Private availability is dependent on customer infra but Redwood supports operational runbooks and on-call integration.
[09:02] Priya Singh: Are there any known limitations integrating with Elastic's vector capabilities?
[09:07] Rohit Patel: Elastic vector search is okay for smaller corpora but at scale specialized vector DBs typically perform better. Indexing strategies and shard sizes matter; we'll include best-practice docs.
[09:20] Liam O'Connor: About data retention — some clients require vector deletion on request; how is that handled?
[09:25] Rohit Patel: We support deletions through APIs and on Private you control the data lifecycle. For Hosted/Dedicated we can set retention policies and provide audit logs showing deletes.
[09:36] Maya Chen: Great. Any notes about encryption in transit between Redwood and vector DB if we're using a 3rd-party DB?
[09:42] Rohit Patel: Always use mTLS or private links; for Dedicated/Private we recommend peered networks to avoid public routes.
[09:50] Priya Singh: For the benchmark, what metrics should we collect?
[09:53] Rohit Patel: Collect QPS, p50/p90/p99 latency for recall and rerank, CPU/GPU utilization, token counts, and embedding throughput (embeds/sec). Also quality metrics like MRR or nDCG on your eval set.
[10:08] Liam O'Connor: We'll provide a labeled eval set (2k queries) for quality checks.
[10:12] Ava Martinez: Perfect. We'll put together the project plan: initial pilot, two-week benchmarking, then production roll.
[10:19] Maya Chen: Timeline — we want pilot in 2 weeks and maybe production in 8-10 weeks depending on results.
[10:25] Ava Martinez: Sounds reasonable. We'll follow up with the docs and pricing.
[10:29] Rohit Patel: I'll also include a suggested index config for Qdrant and Milvus for 1024-d vectors.
[10:36] Priya Singh: Any compliance docs you can send today?
[10:39] Ava Martinez: Yes, I'll attach SOC2 whitepaper and the KMS integration doc after this call.
[10:44] Maya Chen: One last question — do you support version pinning for models during rollouts?
[10:49] Rohit Patel: Yep, you can pin model versions and do canary rollouts with automatic fallback.
[10:54] Priya Singh: Great.
[10:56] Ava Martinez: Ok recap and next steps: Ava send pricing + security pack; Rohit send benchmark templates + index configs; Maya share sample dataset and QPS targets. We'll schedule the benchmark kickoff for next week if that works.
[11:15] Maya Chen: Works for us. Thanks everyone.
[11:18] Liam O'Connor: Thanks.
[11:20] Ava Martinez: Thanks all.
[11:22] End of meeting.

Notes on transcript quality: auto transcription had occasional name garbling (e.g., "Roh it" vs Rohit) and some technical terms mis-transcribed (KV cache -> KV cash) — manual cleanup applied lightly.
